lessons.title: Do the steps take turns flashing?
lessons.summary: Watch a full rotation. Bright flashes switching between different facets can feel lively; a large group of steps going dark together can leave the stone looking quiet.
lessons.prompt: Compare how much of the diamond changes at once. Do the centre and outer steps keep taking turns?

examples.label: Lively example
examples.comment: Karl_K praised its face-up pattern and motion (#51); the buyer described crisp flashes after purchase (#45/#48).

examples.label: Broad simultaneous darkness
examples.comment: 0-0-0 advised against it after the buyer spotted large areas switching off together (#13–#14).

lessons.title: Does the middle stay awake?
lessons.summary: Look under the table, not just around the bright outer edge. A relatively static middle may matter even when the outer steps are busy.
lessons.prompt: Watch the central steps during rotation. Is there changing light return or an area that rarely participates?

examples.label: More active reference
examples.comment: Karl_K liked the movement and face-up design (#51). This is not a measured centre-by-centre benchmark.

examples.label: Quiet centre
examples.comment: Ibrakeforpossums specifically noticed a relatively static middle in the 2.54ct candidate (#40).

lessons.title: Does an area flash, or stay see-through?
lessons.summary: Tilt the stone slowly. Some grey or dark regions are reflections or temporary contrast; persistently transparent under-table steps can instead signal light leakage.
lessons.prompt: Can the weak-looking steps flash on and off as you move? Does stronger tilt reveal a view through the stone?

examples.label: Leakage concern
examples.comment: 0-0-0 identified under-table steps that did not flash on rotation and stronger-tilt through-view (#29/#32).

examples.label: Reflection may mimic leakage
examples.comment: 0-0-0 cautioned that reflections of the surroundings can resemble tilt windowing in the purchased stone (#54).

annotated_source.label: See the buyer's outlined screenshot and expert reply (#31–#32)

lessons.title: Is the darkness useful contrast?
lessons.summary: Dark facets are not automatically bad. Controlled contrast can give step cuts depth and structure, while excessive face-up obstruction or prolonged darkness may overwhelm the pattern.
lessons.prompt: Compare the face-up pattern, then rotate. Does contrast alternate into bright flashes—or linger across too much of the stone?

examples.label: Stronger obstruction
examples.comment: 0-0-0 saw more face-up obstruction than preferred, but acknowledged different tastes for contrast (#17).

examples.label: Promising, with reservations
examples.comment: 0-0-0 preferred its cut; lovedogs worried about darkness at some angles; Karl_K saw potential (#20–#28).
